answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I emptied the hand except for Firework Finale. Kaboom! into Seapunk for 7, Fwoosh! for 8, Bang Bang! for 5 twice into the only body on the field for 10, and then Duck and Cover with my last energy for 5 Block. That is 25 damage, taking Seapunk from 45 to 20, and it turns the incoming 11 into 6, so I end the turn at 38 of 62 instead of 33. The reason I ended up here is that the three Spark cards happen to sit on the same exchange rate: Fwoosh! is 8 for one Spark, Bang Bang! is 10 for two, and together they are exactly 18 for three Sparks, which is exactly what Firework Finale buys for the same three. Since the damage is a tie, everything else broke it. The two-card version leaves both cards in my deck instead of exhausting one, and it puts three separate Pyro applications on the enemy instead of one, and it does not gamble on my only enemy dying mid-card. Kaboom! and Duck and Cover are not competing for anything - I have 3 energy, they cost 1 each, and there is nothing else on the page to spend energy on - so both simply get played.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: The real alternative was Firework Finale plus Kaboom! plus Duck and Cover: 18 + 7 = 25 damage, the same 25, with a card left over in hand. I looked at that one properly rather than dismissing it, because a single 18-damage hit is not always the same as 8 + 5 + 5 - if the enemy had a threshold effect, or if some kind of per-hit mitigation existed, the shapes would diverge. Nothing on this page gives Seapunk any such text, so the two lines collapse to the same number and I picked the one that keeps a card and stacks more Pyro. I also briefly weighed holding Duck and Cover to keep a Block card for a later, bigger telegraph, and holding Sparks rather than spending them all. Both of those died fast: Block does not carry across turns in anything this page tells me, my energy has no other outlet, and there is no Spark income printed anywhere here, so a banked Spark is just damage I did not deal.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up Firework Finale as a live option for the rest of the fight in the sense that it is now stranded - my Spark bank is 0 and the page tells me nothing about how Sparks come back, so a card that demands three of them may sit dead in my hand for several turns. If Sparks refill generously, that is nothing; if they trickle, I have kept a card I cannot cast and spent the two I could recast cheaply, which is the inverse of what I want. It also gave up the option of dealing all 18 in one packet, which matters if Seapunk turns out to have something that punishes being hit repeatedly, and it gave up all defensive flexibility: I am at 0 Block going into next turn with nothing banked and no cards left except an uncastable Finale, so whatever the next telegraph is, I meet it with a fresh draw and no cushion.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes, but only at the edges - the damage half of the turn is untouchable. Against a non-attacking intent, a buff or a block or a debuff telegraph, I would drop Duck and Cover entirely and end the turn with the energy unspent, since 5 Block against nothing is pure waste and there is at least a chance the card is worth more next turn when something is actually swinging at me. Against a much larger attack, say 25 or 30, the line would also not change but for a different reason: 5 Block is all the mitigation this hand can produce, so I would still play it, still dump everything, and just race. The three Spark cards and Kaboom! are effectively forced no matter what Seapunk is doing - I have exactly one target, exactly one way to convert 3 Sparks into 18 damage, and no defensive option large enough to make turtling a real plan. So the intent moves one card, and only one card.

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`

The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
